project.name: Knotz Raven Mayhem
project.productGoal: Move Knotz Raven Mayhem from a lives-gated arcade run into a stage-grading arcade campaign where players can keep seeing later content while still being ranked on performance.
project.v1ScopeDecision: Local records and local progression only. Online leaderboards, databases, backend accounts, cloud saves, and service-worker/offline caching remain deferred beyond v1.

handoffSummary.nextTeamMission: Own the major progression conversion from lives-based failure to stage grades, star ratings, grade-aware rewards, and stage transitions that advance even after low-performance clears.
handoffSummary.whyThisMatters: The game has become visually strong and mechanically more demanding, especially with late-stage enemy pressure and boss fights. Players are not reliably reaching later stages under the current lives model. A grading system lets the full 9-stage arc be experienced while preserving mastery goals through stars, score, coins, records, and upgrade incentives.
handoffSummary.workingBaseline: Preserve the current desktop, iPad, landscape-phone, VFX, boss, Jackpot Alley, armory, local save, release-shell, and GitHub Pages baseline while changing progression rules. Do not restart mobile/PWA or visual-polish workstreams.

currentState.summary: The original raven click-target prototype is now a Phaser 3 + TypeScript + Vite arcade shooter with 9 named stages, bosses, Jackpot Alley, armory progression, local saves, DOM overlays, landscape-first mobile layout, SEO/PWA shell, release verification scripts, procedural stage art/audio, pooled transient VFX, shader-style screen polish, weapon/enemy impact signatures, stage atmosphere, boss spectacle, and improved Raven King behavior.

implementedContent.stages: 9 named stages with different spawn pools, palettes, speed multipliers, rewards, procedural set dressing, Jackpot Alley bonus pacing, overflow scaling after the final named stage, and field-drain stage transitions that wait for active ravens and powerups before showing stage clear.
implementedContent.enemies: 11 enemy definitions: normal, fast, golden, armored, mini, shield, splitter, dive, wraith, brute, and boss. Stage pools reveal enemy types gradually across the full 9-stage arc.
implementedContent.bosses: The Raven King appears on boss stages, is vertically clamped inside a fair arena lane, has boss warning/pressure/defeat presentation, and now spits mini ravens from a clamped mouth position with active boss-minion caps.
implementedContent.weapons: 4 guns: Quarter Pistol, Burst Rifle, Scattergun, Arc Laser. Weapon-specific muzzle, trace, impact, and reticle feedback are implemented.
implementedContent.assistChips: 4 Assist Chip unlocks: Stock Cabinet, Turbo Capacitor, Threat Scanner, Chaos Net. These tune recharge feel and target forgiveness while the live reticle identity follows the equipped gun.
implementedContent.currentUpgrades: 4 permanent upgrade tracks currently exist: cooldown, combo window, starting lives, and payout scaling. The starting-lives upgrade is the main upgrade that must be redesigned for the grading-system conversion.
implementedContent.powerups: 6 powerups: slow-mo, multi-shot, score boost, extra life, overdrive, coin rush. Extra life is also affected by the grading-system conversion and should be redesigned or retired.
implementedContent.audio: Procedural WebAudio with menu/run/boss modes, stage-aware motifs, weapon-specific shots, enemy-specific hit cues, powerup cues, boss warning/defeat stings, stage clear, miss, and game over. AudioContext creation is gated until a real user gesture.
implementedContent.visuals: Seed raven/explosion assets plus procedural stage set dressing, cabinet HUD, stage atmosphere overlays, screen polish, weapon-driven reticles, cooldown feedback, projectile traces, scoring bursts, coin showers, Jackpot Alley FX, boss FX, powerup field FX, and pooled transient graphics for long-session performance.
implementedContent.mobile: Landscape-first mobile is the accepted mobile direction. Portrait phones show a rotate gate, the manifest requests landscape, HUD density and enemy visual scale are reduced for phone landscape, and Armory uses a phone-landscape page scroll model.
implementedContent.releaseOps: Release verification scripts, balance report, SEO/release-shell asset checks, served dist smoke for /Knotz-Raven-Mayhem/, GitHub Actions CI, and manual GitHub Pages deployment workflow are in place.
implementedContent.pwaShell: index.html and public/ include mobile web app tags, icons, manifest.webmanifest, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, social-preview.png, and canonical metadata. Manifest uses id './', start_url './', scope './', display 'standalone', and orientation 'landscape'.

currentProgressionProblem.problem: The current run model is lives-gated. Missed non-bonus ravens call run.loseLife(), and 0 lives ends the run. Because the game is harder now, players can lose access to later stages instead of receiving a poor stage grade and continuing.
currentProgressionProblem.targetChange: Stages should advance after the spawn quota and field drain complete, even when the player misses many ravens. Misses should lower grade, rewards, and records rather than hard-stopping the run.
recommendedGradeScale: 5 stars: 90% or higher grade-eligible kill percentage.
1 star: below 60%, still a stage pass unless the player quits or a new explicit failure rule is approved.
currentProgressionProblem.importantNuance: Do not calculate stars by blindly using total stageKills divided by stageTargetKills. Splitter children, boss-spit mini ravens, and possibly future bonus spawns can inflate kills. Track grade-eligible spawned enemies and grade-eligible kills explicitly, then clamp percentages to 100%.
currentProgressionProblem.bossStages: Boss stages should no longer be life-gated. The boss can remain a required objective, but missed ravens and boss-spit minions should hurt grade/rewards rather than causing game over. If boss duration becomes too long, tune boss health/spit cadence separately instead of reintroducing lives as the main progression gate.

latestPlaytestUpdate.summary: The game looks and feels substantially better after VFX, screen polish, boss spectacle, and boss-spit work. The next product-level issue is progression accessibility: the game is hard enough that the lives model blocks many players from seeing later levels.
acceptedSignals: Desktop and iPad gameplay are strong.
The VFX and shader-style presentation work should be preserved.
Raven King boss clamp and boss-spit behavior should be preserved unless playtesting shows difficulty spikes.
Armory and local progression remain important; the grading system should feed that loop rather than replacing it.
remainingValidation: Design and implement stage-grade data, UI, rewards, and records.
Playtest whether low-grade stage advancement keeps the game exciting without making mastery feel irrelevant.
Retest boss stages after lives are removed because boss-spit pressure will shift from survival pressure to grade pressure.

Run DOCS/RELEASE-QA-CHECKLIST.md end to end after the grading conversion.

nextTeamPrimaryFocus.theme: Stage grading, star ratings, reward conversion, and lives-system removal.

priorityOrder.title: Define the grade model and data contract
details: Add an explicit stage-grade model instead of deriving grades from existing total kills.
Recommended fields: gradeEligibleSpawned, gradeEligibleKilled, escapedGradeEligible, optionalKills, stageAccuracy, starCount, gradeLabel, and gradePercent.
Use 5 stars for 90%+, 4 for 80%+, 3 for 70%+, 2 for 60%+, and 1 below 60%.
Decide whether boss death is a required objective. Recommended: boss must be defeated, but misses/minions only lower grade.
Document whether bonus-stage Jackpot Raven misses affect grade, coins only, or a separate bonus grade.

priorityOrder.title: Replace lives as the progression gate
details: Change missed non-bonus ravens in GameScene.ts from loseLife/endRun into escaped/missed grade accounting.
Keep stage flow based on spawn quota plus field clear, then show stage clear with a grade rather than ending the run.
Remove or redesign low-life screen polish and HUD life pips.
Update RunState.ts so per-stage grade state resets on startStage() and snapshots expose grade fields.
Preserve combo reset and miss feedback on misses so skill still matters.

priorityOrder.title: Revamp stage-clear, game-over, and records UI
details: Stage clear should show stars, grade percentage, killed/escaped grade-eligible enemies, accuracy, combo, reward coins, and next-stage preview.
Game over should become a run summary, quit summary, or end-of-arc recap rather than a lives failure screen.
Records should track best grade per stage, total stars, best full-run grade, and possibly perfect-stage count.
HUD should show current stage grade trend or kill percentage instead of life pips.
Keep DOM overlays for text-heavy summaries; do not move this UI into Phaser canvas.

priorityOrder.title: Redesign lives-related progression
details: Recommended: keep the internal upgrade id thickJacket for save compatibility but rename it to a grading-era upgrade such as Recovery Matrix, Stage Curve, or Grade Buffer.
Suggested mechanic: each rank grants a small per-stage grade buffer, forgiveness for the first escaped raven, or a minimum reward floor without granting free 5-star grades.
Do not make the upgrade simply raise star ratings for free; mastery should still require strong play.
Extra Life powerup should become a grading-era powerup such as Recovery Token, Grade Shield, Combo Restore, or Retake Spark.
If UpgradeId/stat names change, update save normalization and test returning saves carefully.

priorityOrder.title: Retune rewards and release confidence
details: Grade should affect coins, records, stage medals, and upgrade recommendations.
Run npm run balance:report after changing rewards, economy, stage flow, enemy accounting, boss behavior, or upgrades.
Run npm run typecheck and npm run build after code changes.
Run npm run release:check and npm run release:smoke after build, asset, manifest, release-shell, or dist-path changes.
Run npm run release:verify before handoff or release-candidate tagging.

architecturePointers.runtime: src/main.ts creates the Phaser game with BootScene, AttractScene, and GameScene and imports src/styles.css.
architecturePointers.gameplayScene: src/game/scenes/GameScene.ts owns active run spawning, input, hit resolution, misses, stage flow, boss flow, stage clear, game over, procedural effects, pooled transient effects, and HUD dispatch. Current lives loss happens here when non-boss enemies leave screen.
architecturePointers.runState: src/game/systems/RunState.ts owns lives, maxLives, loseLife(), addLife(), stageKills, stageTargetKills, combo, accuracy, active powerups, weapon cooldown, and RunSnapshot creation. This should own or expose grade state.
architecturePointers.types: src/game/types.ts defines UpgradeId, UpgradeDefinition.stat, PlayerStats.startingLives, RunSnapshot lives/maxLives fields, RunRewards, and StageClearSummary. Grade fields and stat replacements start here.
architecturePointers.uiLayer: src/ui/app.ts renders DOM overlays for attract, armory, records, options, HUD, stage clear, pause, and game over. Life pips, stage-clear stats, game-over stats, and upgrade stat labels live here.
architecturePointers.uiEvents: src/ui/events.ts carries UiState payloads from Phaser scenes to DOM UI. Update this when RunSnapshot or StageClearSummary gains grade fields.
architecturePointers.upgrades: src/game/data/upgrades.ts defines Thick Jacket as starting-lives today. Rename/rework carefully; keep internal id if preserving saves.
architecturePointers.progression: src/game/systems/progression.ts maps save upgrades into PlayerStats. It currently converts thickJacket ranks into startingLives.
architecturePointers.tuning: src/game/data/tuning.ts contains baseStartingLives, thickJacketRanksPerLife, extraLifeOverflowCap, accuracy bonus, economy, powerup, presentation, and overflow tuning. Grade thresholds and grade payout multipliers can live here.
architecturePointers.save: src/game/save.ts normalizes localStorage save data, applies purchases/rewards, calculates run rewards, and normalizes upgrade ranks. Any save shape or UpgradeId/stat change must preserve returning saves.
architecturePointers.balance: scripts/report-balance.mjs reads live TypeScript data and estimates stage pacing, rewards, and economy costs. Update it when grade payouts or upgrade identities change.
architecturePointers.releaseShell: index.html and public/ own SEO, Open Graph/Twitter metadata, favicon/app icons, web manifest, social preview images, mobile web app tags, robots, and sitemap.
architecturePointers.releaseChecks: scripts/check-release.mjs validates dist files, release-shell metadata, and public web kit assets. scripts/smoke-dist.mjs serves dist from /Knotz-Raven-Mayhem/ and fetches linked assets, seed assets, and release-shell assets.

githubPagesDeploymentNote.currentStatus: The correct publish path remains manual Deploy GitHub Pages on master after release verification is green. CI verification alone does not publish.
githubPagesDeploymentNote.why: The classic Pages branch/folder source can show a blank white screen after the Vite migration because it may serve stale or mismatched static output. The Actions deployment uploads the freshly built dist artifact.

implementationGuidance: The next team's main mission is not more VFX. It is the progression conversion from lives to stage grades.
Preserve the accepted landscape-mobile baseline and retest it after HUD/stage-clear changes.
Do not drift into online leaderboards, accounts, databases, cloud systems, or service-worker caching for this grading pass.
Do not make low grades block progression; use stars, records, coins, and upgrade recommendations as the pressure loop.
Track grade-eligible enemies explicitly. Boss-spit mini ravens, splitter children, bonus spawns, and future optional threats should not accidentally inflate grade percentage.
Keep boss fights challenging, but remove lives as the thing that prevents players from seeing later stages.
Keep current VFX, boss clamp/spit behavior, stage atmosphere, weapon feedback, and release-shell work unless a grading bug requires a targeted change.
Use DOM overlays for text-heavy grading UI such as stage-clear summaries, run recap, records, upgrade recommendations, and grade explanations.
If save shape changes, update normalization in src/game/save.ts and test returning-save behavior manually.
After grade/reward/tuning changes, rerun npm run balance:report and update DOCS/BALANCE-NOTES.md if the baseline changes materially.
After runtime, asset, manifest, release-shell, Vite config, or deploy-script changes, run npm run release:verify before handoff.
After deployment, validate the live GitHub Pages URL in a fresh browser profile or private window.
openDesignQuestions: Should 1 star always advance the player, or should there be a separate explicit quit/abandon/failure state?
Should boss defeat be mandatory for boss-stage progression, or should boss stages also grade out after a time/spawn quota?
Should boss-spit mini ravens affect grade directly, only combo/score, or a separate boss-pressure bonus?
What should Thick Jacket become: grade buffer, recovery token, reward floor, combo recovery, or miss forgiveness?
What should Extra Life become in the new system?
Should grade-based rewards multiply coins, unlock stage medals, affect armory recommendations, or all three?
Should records show best star count per stage, total stars, full-run average grade, perfect clears, or a cabinet-style report card?
What is the desired target experience for newer players: reach all 9 stages in one session with low grades, or reach late stages over several upgraded runs?
